structured_output.what_is_happening: This is one of at least 11 "Degens Dollars On Solana" ($DDOS) tokens launched within minutes of each other. They all appear to react to a Polymarket X post (the packet's GeckoTerminal link points to Polymarket/status/2103653913823961467), which I could not read (HTTP 402). This contract is a Meteora pair created at 01:44Z. It has about $22k market cap, about $30k of reported liquidity, and $535k of volume in 12 minutes. A pump.fun version (zpTj...pump) created 85 seconds later is already at about $115k market cap and looks like the one people mean. Several other copies look almost identical: about $20k market cap, about $29k liquidity and heavy volume. That pattern suggests a clone factory.

narrative.description: The name seems to play on a Polymarket tweet (possibly a joke about 'DDOS' / degens). I could not see what the tweet says.
narrative.why_spreading: A Polymarket post from a major account set off a race of copycat launches. Attention is spread across many clones, and the pump.fun version is leading.

token_connection.competing_tokens: zpTj1yA68UauZqdz5276qrpTV7ALkeoLp9LLa7Bpump ($115k mcap, $357k h1 volume) is the clear leader. FDT6, H3RU, E2t6 and 9zMg are near-identical Meteora clones at about $20k mcap with about $29k liquidity. 6hHJ, an earlier 'Degen Dollars' version, already has zero liquidity.

authenticity.evidence: GMGN counts 38 bundler wallets, and top bundler traders hold 31%. There are 1,462 unique buyers but only 58 unique sellers across 4,000+ transactions, which looks like bots. Several sibling clones share the same liquidity-above-market-cap and heavy-volume shape. The creator holds 68.68% of supply, and the LP is 100% unlocked.
